Enterprise Access to ArcGIS Pro

This Section describes the procedure to connect to the MDTA Enterprise GIS through ArcGIS Pro. Please note that ArcGIS Pro must first be installed on your computer to continue with this guide—please contact the MDTA HelpDesk for assistance

  1. Open ArcGIS Pro
  2. Click "Settings" in the lower left-hand corner of the ArcGIS Pro splash screen
  3. Click the "Portals"menu on the left-hand side of the screen
  4. Click the "Add Portal" button below the list of available ArcGIS portals. (ArcGIS Online should be available)
  5. Enter the MDTA ArcGIS Enterprise Portal URL in the dialog box (https://gis.mdta.maryland.com/portal)

Follow the steps below to switch the active Portal.

  1. Open ArcGIS Pro
  2. With or without a project open, click the drop-down menu in the upper right-hand corner
  3. From the drop-down menu, you can get to the "Portals" screen by clicking "Manage Portaldescriptions", or you can switch your active portal by clicking the "Switch Active Portal" and choosing another portal.

To browse items in the Portal:

  1. Open a project in ArcGIS Pro
  2. Click the "View" tab along the top of the ribbon
  3. Under the "View" tab, click the "Catalog Pane" button
  4. In the "Catalog Pane" click "Portal" along the top of the window
  5. You can navigate and filter through organizational content by hiding folders, sorting, filtering, and searching using the search bar
  6. By clicking on the icon-starts, you can view your content, content in groups of which are a member of, items throughout the portal, and items contained in ESRI's Living Atlas (Living Atlas items are items that ESRI has shared with all users of ArcGIS—they contain various maps, layers, and applications that you may use within your projects)
  7. You may also search for portal items by name by using the search bar
  1. You can add a portal item to a map in your project by either dragging the item from the "Catalog Pane" to your map, or by right-clicking on the item and clicking and then clicking "Add to Current Map" or "Add to New" and choose a new map or scene.

This is a sandbox ArcGIS Server site where the users will be freely testing their applications and services. Typically, the development site runs on a small machine using an Esri Developer Network (EDN) license for ArcGIS Server. Once changes are validated on the development site, they will be applied to the staging site.

In dev deployment, the software components are installed on total of 2 machines including the Database Server.

This ArcGIS Server site is a clone of the production site. Testing at this level results in a decision to apply the changes on the production site or reject the changes and wait for a new iteration from the development site. The staging site is not used for development, just performance and functional testing.

Esri provides staging licenses for ArcGIS Server users at a lower cost than production licenses. In test deployment, the software components are installed on total of 4 machines including Database Server.

Production (PROD)

This is the site actually supports business workflows, the site accessed by real users. Absolutely no development or testing occurs on this site. Only changes that have passed the scrutiny of testing on the staging site are applied to the production site. In production the functionality and capacity of the base Enterprise deployment is extended with two additional servers

In production deployment, the software components are installed on total of 6 machines including Database Server. This requires 3 ArcGIS Enterprise 10.9.1 and licenses 1 SQL Server 2016 license.

As is is possible that our user base and activity increases, the components of our base ArcGIS Enterprise deployment may need to be scaled out with additional resources.

The four components of ArcGIS Enterprise work together to provide comprehensive functionality for web mapping, image exploitation, real-time data handling, large-volume batch analysis, and spatial data science:

  • ArcGIS Server powers mapping and analysis in your GIS, including several specialized server roles, and scales dynamically to support traffic.
  • The ArcGIS Enterprise portal is the central hub where users create, share, and manage maps, apps, and spatial data, and share them with collaborators.
  • ArcGIS Data Store provides nimble data storage for the hosting server used with your deployment.
  • ArcGIS Web Adaptor integrates ArcGIS Server and Portal for ArcGIS with your existing web servers and your organization's security infrastructure.

A base ArcGIS Enterprise deployment is the minimum setup, combining all four ArcGIS Enterprise components. MDOT MDTA Enterprise GIS has been scaled to meet the orgaizaton's needs and can be scaled further as the need arises.

The ArcGIS Server component of ArcGIS Enterprise is licensed by CPU cores. Cores are part of the computer's CPU (Central Processing Unit) that determines the number of instructions that can be processed at a given time. A 4-core processor can handle four sets of instructions at once. Many modern CPUs further support a technology known as hyper-threading that allows a single core to run multiple concurrent sets of instructions. Hyper-threads do not count towards the licensed cores.

Licensed cores can be counted by physical cores or virtual cores, whichever is more advantageous to you. The minimum purchase for ArcGIS Enterprise is an "up-to-4 core" license* which can be installed on a two or four core machine. If your machine has more than 4 cores (physical or virtual), you can purchase additional cores, or virtualize the machine so that the 4-core license of ArcGIS Enterprise is only installed on 4 (virtual) cores and thereby satisfies the license requirement.

If a 4-core license is installed on an 8-core physical machine without virtualization, then ArcGIS Enterprise will use all 8 cores and would be in violation of the license agreement until you purchase a license for the four "additional cores". For example:

  1. A 4-core physical machine would use an "up-to-4 core" license for ArcGIS Enterprise.
  2. If that same machine is virtualized using hyper-threading technology whereby the virtual core count is equivalent to 8 cores, it would still only require an "up-to-4 core" ArcGIS Enterprise license since there are only 4 physical cores on the machine.
  3. An 8-core physical machine would use and "up-to-4 core" license for ArcGIS Enterprise plus 4 "additional cores" so that all 8 cores are licensed.
  4. If that same machine is virtualized so that there are equivalent to two (2) 4-core virtual machines, a 4-core ArcGIS Enterprise license could be installed on one of the virtual machines, leaving the other 4-core VM for other uses

This section is for guidance only. The below content is subject to change.

  1. Only 64-bit operating systems satisfy the minimum operating system requirements. Support is not provided for 32-bit operating systems; the setup will only proceed if the operating system is 64-bit.
  2. Machines with an underscore (_) in their names are not supported. ArcGIS Server will not install on servers that have an underscore in the host name.
  3. ArcGIS Server is not supported on domain controllers. Installing ArcGIS Server on a domain controller may adversely affect functionality.
  4. We must have a certificate from a trusted certificate authority (CA) and configure the server to use it. This could be a domain certificate issued by MDTA or a CA-signed certificate.
  5. The following virtualization environments are known to perform well with ArcGIS Enterprise and its components:
    • VMware vSphere 6.5, 6.7
    • Microsoft Hyper-V

Portal Authentication

MDTA will secure access to the portal using Windows Active Directory and built-in accounts (For contractors who are not in MDTA domain). This has been configured in the test environment.

Since MDTA would like to allow access to the portal using both enterprise and built-in identity stores, the ArcGIS Portal-tier authentication is best suited for this purpose. This was achieved by configuring the portal with MDTA's Windows Active Directory. When a user accesses the portal sign-in page, they will be able to log in using either enterprise credentials or built-in credentials. Enterprise users will be required to enter their account credentials each time they log in to the portal; automatic sign on will not be available.

Firewall and Ports

The below diagram specifically shows the TCP traffic through the ports:

Additional communication details on the GIS components

  • The ArcGIS Web Adaptor in the perimeter network receives internet or MDTA network requests through a common port 443. A firewall prevents access through any other ports. Then ArcGIS Web Adaptor sends the request to the secure internal network through another firewall over the ArcGIS Portal port 7443 or ArcGIS Server port 6443.
  • The GIS servers and other ArcGIS Enterprise components reside in the secure internal network. A request entering the secure network must come from ArcGIS Web Adaptor and pass through a firewall. A response leaving the secure network returns to the client the same way it arrived. First, the response passes back through the firewall to ArcGIS Web Adaptor. Then ArcGIS Web Adaptor sends it through another firewall to the client.

If a machine in the DMZ somehow becomes compromised, the second firewall reduces the chance that the affected machine can harm machines in the internal network.

Geodatabase Administration

Version 1.4 - Last Updated 2/12/2021

Introduction

At MDTA, there isn't any dedicated GIS DBA who can perform the administration tasks related to the DB. Therefore, the permissions documented here is a result of agreed procedures and rights between DBA and the GIS team and based on ESRI's recommendation mentioned in the following link: here

There are two parts of administration when it comes to Geodatabases for a GIS admin. First is the geodatabase administration of system tables, views, procedures etc. this is handled by sde user as mentioned in detail below. The other part of it is supporting customers if they have a need of new DB or they need to create or restore a backup etc. since these are more serious permissions and at MDTA after the discussions with DBAs, GIS admins will have permissions to do these tasks only up to test environment.

In Microsoft SQL Server, the geodatabase administrator can be either a user named "sde" or a login that is mapped to the "dbo" user in the database that contains the geodatabase. The geodatabase administrator is responsible for the administration of the following:

  • Geodatabase system tables, triggers, views, and procedures
  • The DEFAULT geodatabase version

Because the geodatabase administrator owns all the geodatabase system files, directories, and tables, the geodatabase administrator account must be created before you can create a geodatabase. To create a sde-schema geodatabase, you must have a user named "sde" in the database. At MDTA we are using sde schema for creating the geodatabase administrator and geodatabase.

From time to time GIS team needs to create Enterprise Geodatabases (GDBs) depending on the needs of the other divisions.
Permissions for GIS Admin in Dev

Currently GIS team has ability to create Enterprise GDBs only in Dev. The following two users and the privileges associated with them allows GIS Admins to perform and GIS maintenance, creation or upgrade related tasks in this environment:

  1. GIS_Admin
  2. sde
 Permissions for GIS Admins in Test

In Test GIS admins will have some elevated privileges for the "sde" user and will also have a GIS Admins (AD account of Luv Arora) for creating new Databases, creating backups and restoring backups. But since it's a cluster it is GIS admins responsibility to notify DBAs of any new DB that needs to be synchronized on the cluster. The two users that are used for GIS administration will be one of the current GIS_Admin and the other one is "sde". In test the "sde" will have rights up to processadmin based on ESRIs recommendation as mentioned below:

  • The geodatabase administrator (the "sde" user) in a sde-schema geodatabase must be added to the processadmin fixed server role and granted VIEW DEFINITION privileges on the database to drop geodatabase connections.

The "sde" user will not own data in the geodatabase outside of the system objects, the "sde" user only needs to be able to connect to the geodatabase once the geodatabase has been created. However, when the geodatabase needs to be upgraded or if the "sde" user needs to kill connections or view all database users, additional privileges are required.

 Permissions for GIS Admins in Production

In production GIS admins will have elevated privileges for the "sde" user same as test but GIS admins AD account will not have elevated permissions. Anything that needs to be pushed to production needs to go through DBAs. They will be responsible for creating the backup from test and restore it in production and they will also be responsible for synchronizing the DB in the cluster. The "sde" will still have rights up to processadmin based on ESRIs recommendation.

ESRI recommends as mentioned in this linkabove that the geodatabase administrator's schema only be used to store the geodatabase repository. Therefore, separate users and schemas are created to store datasets such as feature classes and tables. These SQL Server logins/database users are known as "data owners". Following the practice of storing only geodatabase system objects in the geodatabase administrator's schema simplifies the management of the geodatabase and makes it easier to delete the geodatabase from the database if it is ever decided to do so.

GIS Data Viewer Guide

User Guides

The user guide widget will take you to a page that will display links to videos explaining the main features of the application.

Clicking any of the links will open a video on the selected topic in YouTube. You can also click on the link to access the MDTA GIS Data View playlist.

Navigation

Upon logging into the system, users will see the following set of widget icons on the bottom left of the screen. These widgets allow the users to navigate through the map displayed on the screen.

  • To zoom in click the widget. If the user clicks on this widget more than once the map will continue to zoom in.
  • To zoom out, click the widget. If the user clicks on this widget more than once the map will continue to zoom out. If the user has a mouse with a scroll wheel, it will act as a zoom in and zoom out. Scrolling up will zoom in. Scrolling down will zoom out.
  • To get back to the original view, click the widget.
  • Clicking on the widget works like a back button. It will take the user back to the previous view of the map. Clicking will take the user to a screen they looked at after the one they are on. This widget will be greyed out if there are no views to see.
  • To minimize any window, click the ellipse (#2) in the upper right corner. When this is done, the window will be displayed smaller.
  • To restore the window, click the ellipse at the bottom of the widget.
  • Click the (#3) in the upper right corner to close a widget.
  • To change the settings for an active widget, click the gear widget (#1). When the user clicks the settings widget, the setting options will be displayed.
  • If the user wants to search by Asset ID, Barcode or Legacy ID, they can click the search button which will look grey before becoming active. After the user clicks the widget, it will show as dark blue and a "Please enter a search term" text box will be displayed for the user to enter an item to run a search.
  • If what is searched cannot be found, the user will receive the following message: "No Results: There were no results found for "<search criteria>".
  • If the user zooms in close enough on the map, the map will change to the most current aerial photographic view of Maryland, provided by Maryland iMap.
  • The icon in the lower right corner of a screen indicates that the active window can be made larger/smaller by clicking the widget and dragging the corner.

Toggle Layers

This will allow users to turn on or off the dataset for a particular office or division. By default, only reference layers are turned on. Individual layers are grouped by subject. The following data layer widgets are available to the user:

  • Drainage
  • Electrical
  • Facilities
  • ITS
  • Lighting
  • National Pollutant Discharge Elimination System (NPDES
  • Real Estate
  • Structure
  • Utilities
  • Reference Data

The first time the user clicks on a toggle layer button the background color of the icon will be dark blue indicating that it's turned on.

When the layers are turned on, they will appear in the Legend. The map must be zoomed into that layer's active zoom extent in order to see the layers on the Legend.

Turning all layers on or off applies to all layers within the group. In the left-side of the screen shot shown left, "Turn all layers on" is active. On the right-side is showing what the list looks like when "Turn all layers off" is active.

To search for a specific layer while a widget is active, click the search tool in the upper right corner of the layer widget, then start typing the name of the layer to run a search on. As text is entered, matching layers will be displayed.

Some layers are divided into MDTA owned, non-MDTA owner and removed.

Each layer will have settings that can be set by the user. These setting include:

  • Set visibility range
  • Disable pop-up
  • View in attribute table
  • Show item detail

Note - Click the following URL to go to the video tutorial: https://youtu.be/wmCQCqwdzWA.

Tools

At the bottom of the GIS Data Viewer page, a group of tool widgets will be displayed.

The first set of widgets are:

  • User Guides
  • Legend
  • Bookmark
  • Group Filter
  • Filter

The next set of widgets are the toggle layer references. The following tools are available:

  • All Layers: The All Layers is a central place where any type of data layer can be toggled on or off.
  • Query Data: This tool can be used to tool to filter data and creates a temporary data layer of filtered data.
  • Select: Users can interactively select features from the layers that are turned on in the map and marked as selectable.
  • Measurement: This widget will allow users to measure a distance or area on the map or obtain location coordinates.
  • Add Data: The user can add data layers from a variety of sources to their view of the application.
  • Basemap Gallery: The user can change the background map data or underlying imagery
  • Print

Legend

Allows users to see a listing of currently displayed features. The items shown on the Legend will be seen on the map.

Bookmarks

Allows users to save a bookmark for quick reference. This is saved in the browser's cache and will be saved if internet history is not deleted. Once the user is zoomed into the area and they would like to bookmark:

  1. Click on the bookmark tool
  2. Type in a name
  3. Click on the plus button.

Users can delete bookmarks as needed by clicking the Delete button at the bottom of the dialog box. There are some pre-defined bookmarks that users can directly zoom into:

Filters

Note: A link to the video tutorial for filters can be found here: https://youtu.be/lj3_Ryjha4g

Group Filters

Group filtering filters all data by a selected facility.

To filter by facility:

  • Click the Group Filter widget
  • Select a facility from the drop down.
  • Click Apply.

To remove the filter, click the Reset button.

Filters

Allows users to filter data by pre-defined filters. Once a user toggles on any of the filters it zooms in to the full extent of that filter.

Users can also define their own filters by clicking the three dots, then clicking the filter icon.

The user will select a layer from the drop down. Then the following options will be displayed so the user can use their own query to create a filter:

When the Add expression button is clicked, the following will be displayed under the Layer selected:

There is a list of objects in the drop down that can be selected from to build an expression to create a filter. Clicking the gear icon to the right of the bottom field, will display a list of options;

  • Value
  • Field
  • Unique

When one of the options is selected, the field will display a list of items related to the option selected.

If Field is selected, a list of fields in the GIS layer will be available to select.

If + Add Set is selected, the system will add 2 expressions that are connected. There will be a drop down with 2 options that the user can selected for the conditional filter. There can be multiple expressions in a set.

  1. All of the following expressions in this set are true
  2. Any of the following expressions in this set are true – Clicking the plus sign next to the "Any of the following..." dropdown adds another expression to the set.

All Layers

Allows users to turn layers on and off in the map. Users can turn additional layers on or off by clicking on the box. If there is a check in the box, the layer is currently turned on. If the box and associated layer name are grayed out, the layer has a scale dependency, and the map is zoomed out too far to see the layer.

An attribute table is available to see more information about the items in the selected area. To see the attribute table, click the arrow at the bottom of the page.

The attribute table will look like this:

If the user wants to see more of the list in the attribute table, click on the line displayed under the arrow to view the attribute table, then drag it up the screen.

Query Data

Querying data creates a temporary layer of data that meets specified criteria.

To query data:

1. Click the widget at the bottom of the screen.

2. Select a layer to query.

3. Select query criteria for the specified layer selected above. These options may change depending on the layer selected in step 2.

The selection statement will be displayed above the Apply button. In this case it's "UPPER(bmp_type) IN (‘FILTERING')"

4. If the user wants to save the query results under a new name, enter the new name in the Result layer name field.

5. Click Apply.

6. The results will display in the Query Data widget listing all features that meet the search criteria. The result layer will be added to the legend.

7. Click any of the features in the results pane to zoom closer to said feature and to open the feature's pop-up window which shows more information on the feature. The teal-colored line is the one that user has clicked on to get the information in the box on the left.

There are 7 options listed for the new layer.

  • Zoom to - If the map extent has been moved away from the query result layer, Zoom to returns to the results layer, changing the zoom level.
  • Pan to - If the map extent has been moved away from the query result layer, Pan to returns to the results layer without changing the zoom level.
  • Flash - Flash highlights visible features by alternating between two colorations or flashing features.
  • Export to CSV file - This option will export all the records on a given table into an CSV file, which can then be opened in Excel.
  • Statistics - If the Statistics option is clicked, a pop up will be displayed showing stats for the selected field.
  • View in Attribute Table - The attribute table will be displayed at the bottom of the page showing the result layer data in table form.
  • Remove this result - Removes the temporary results layer from the map.

Note: See the following URL for a video tutorial: https://youtu.be/rad9UVXJIB4

Select

Allows users to interactively select features from the layers that are turned on in the map and marked as selectable. Once the features are selected, the corresponding records in the attribute table area also selected. To select items on the map:

1. Open the Select widget by clicking at the bottom of the screen.

2. Click the Select button. Select is active when the button is black as shown to the left.

3. Select a section on the map by clicking the mouse, then dragging a square figure on the map. The area drawn on the map will show up in light blue as seen in the following screen shot.

4. After letting go of the mouse, the layers in the light blue are will be marked and the number of the specific layers in that area will be listed on the screen.

Clicking the ellipse (2:00 m on video) provides the following options.

  • Zoom to: If the map extent has been moved away from the query result layer, Zoom to returns to the results layer, changing the zoom level.
  • Pan to: If the map extent has been moved away from the query result layer, Pan to returns to the results layer without changing the zoom level.
  • Export to CSV file: This option will export all the records on a given table into an CSV file, which can then be opened in Excel.
  • Statistics: If the Statistics option is clicked, a pop up will be displayed showing stats for the selected field.
  • Create a layer
    • : A Create Layer pop up will be displayed to enter a name of your choosing. Click OK to save the layer with the name entered. Click the Cancel button to cancel creating the layer.
  • View in Attribute Table: The attribute table will be displayed at the bottom of the page showing more information about the layer.
  • Clear selection: Removes the temporary results layer from the map.

To add features to the selection, hold the Shift button while selecting features.

To remove items from the selection, hold the Ctrl button while dragging over features to be removed.

View in attribute table (3:00)

View in Attribute Table action from the ellipses (…) for the layer is used to open the attribute table for that layer

Click on the row header to highlight a specific row. Hold CTRL and click with the mouse to highlight more than one row

If the column header is clicked, the user can select to sort them in ascending and descending order.

There are 5 options available on each data set when looking at the attribute table. They are:

  • Options
    • Show Selected Records: If rows are selected and this option is picked, only the rows that were highlighted will remain displayed. This option will change to "Show All Records" when only selected records are being displayed.
    • Show Related Records: This option shows additional related information if it exists.
    • Filter: Selecting this option will display the Filter widget. You can then add expressions and / or add sets of expressions to show specific records.
    • Hide / Show Columns: When this option is selected, a list of all the columns available will be displayed on the right side of the screen. By default, all the column headers will be checked. To remove column headers from the table, uncheck the box next to the column to hide. To show the column again, re-check the checkbox. In Figured 5-14, Facility, Location, Route ID and Milepoint columns have been removed, if comparing to the columns displayed in Figures 6-13.
  • Export all to CSV: This option will export all the records on a given table into an CSV file, which can then be opened in Excel.
  • Filter by map extent: Allows users to filter data to the current map area being displayed.
  • Zoom to: If the map extent has been moved away from the query result layer, zoom to returns to the results layer, changing the zoom level
  • Clear selection: Removes the temporary results layer from the map.
  • Refresh: Redisplays the information on the map.

Measurement

Allows users to measure a distance or area on the map or obtain location coordinates. The user will choose to measure either a line or polygon feature. The user will choose the unit of measurement. A single click will place a starting or interim measurement point. Double-clicking will complete the feature.

The user will have the ability to change the Area, Distance and / or Location being measured.

To select Area, the user will have to click on the Area widget. When the user clicks this widget, a drop down will appear to the right of the widgets displayed.

The user will be given the following units of measure options to choose from:

  • Acres
  • Sq. Miles
  • Sq. Kilometers
  • Hectares
  • Sq. Yards
  • Sq. Feet
  • Sq. Feet (US)
  • Sq. Meters

When the user selects to use the Area option, they will use the mouse to select an area on the map to measure. Double click to end the drawing. See the example to the left. The blue outline is what was selected on the map. The circled number on the right is the number of Sq. Feet the area in blue measures.

To change the measurement option to distance the user will have to click the Distance widget

After the user clicks the Distance widget, different options will be displayed in the drop down. Those options are:

  • Miles
  • Kilometers
  • Feet
  • Meters
  • Yards
  • Nautical Miles

If the user selects the Distance tool, they will select a point on the map, then another point on the map. On the right side of the screen, the measuring tool will show how many miles between the points. The example below shows how many miles around the circles building.

Clicking on the Location icon will bring up the last set of options.

Those options are:

  • Degrees (here the user will move the mouse on the screen to get the latitude and longitude numbers). When the user clicks on the map, the first set of numbers will be set. The user must then select another position on the map then click on that position for the 2nd set of latitude and longitude numbers to be set.
  • Degrees, Minutes, Seconds (DMS) If the user wants to clear the measurements at any point, they can click the Clear button under the measurement results.

MDTA GIS Enterprise System Backup and Recovery Information and Procedures

Version 1.3 - last updated 5/7/2023

Introduction

The purpose of this page is to provide information on how data is backed up and how to recover from a partial or full system failure of the GIS system. There are different types of recovery to be used depending upon the scenario.

Backup Information

The ArcGIS Web Adaptor for Portal on the MDOT DMZ (MDTAGBDMZGIS) is backed up nightly by the Transportation Secretaries Office's (TSO) Office of Transportation Technology Services (OTTS) and kept for 36 days.

The following servers will be fully backed up nightly through Rubrik at Brick level.

  • MDTAGISWEB1 - ArcGIS Web Adaptor (ArcGIS Server)
  • MDTAGISWEB2 - Application Server (ArcGIS Server)
  • MDTAGISWEB3 - Application Server (ArcGIS Portal)
  • MDTAGISDSTORE - ArcGIS Data Store
  • MDTAGISBAT1 - Application Server (Batch Server)
  • MDTAGISPOL1 - Application Server (Publish MPA Data)
  • MDTAGISSQL19 - SQL Server - Cluster Node 1
  • MDTAGISSQL20 - SQL Server - Cluster Node 2
  • MDTAGISSQL21 - SQL Server - Cluster Node 3 Disaster Recovery

All backups for the above servers will be kept for 14 days.

SQL Cluster

SQL Server Always-On Availability Group (AAG) on a three-node cluster provides synchronous and asynchronous replication of database between nodes as well as VMWare VCenter/Data Center sites.

Between the 2 ICC nodes there will be a synchronous replication (automatic recovery).

Between the ICC nodes and the JFK node it will be asynchronous replication (manual recovery).

The Datastore for GIS backups are run via scheduled modular scripts. These scripts create tables with logs and tracks the jobs for different backups. This includes tracking the rollover thresholds which are 2-weeks for the GIS datastore. The log files write the commands issued to generate the SQL backup files. These backup files are then copied and stored in a SQL Backup file share directory accessible to all MDTA's SQL DBAs and other DOIT IT Disaster Recovery (DR) personal. File shared file backups are saved for 90 days.

Recovery Point Objectives

A Recovery Point Objective (RPO) is the point in time the system can be recovered to in the event of a system failure. Any data saved in the amount of time between the RPO, and the present time may be lost during recovery. This acceptance should be documented and should be defined by the business stakeholders with guidance from the IT Systems Engineers and Database Administrators. The backup strategy and configuration must support the RPO.

The RPO, in this scenario, given the points listed under Recovery Time Objectives (RTO), an RPO of 2 weeks/14 days is well attainable.

Server configuration back-ups are done nightly. See Server Backups section.

Database back-ups will be done every 12 hours. See SQL Database section.

CIFS and Server Data are backed up every 24 hours, see Datastore Back-Ups section. Since replication of SQL database occurs in near real time replication, using AAG Clusters, an RPO of minutes may be attainable.

Recovery Time Objectives

A Recovery Time Objective (RTO) is the time measured from a system failure event until services are fully restored and functional to the end user. It is, essentially, about downtime and all activities involved in coming up with the total expected recovery time or RTO, such as backup media recall, travel time (if applicable), infrastructure recovery, data restore, service restore, application configuration, test, and validation.

RTO - Recovery Time Objective (Time to bring the system back the full functionality) 24 hours for GIS

RPO - Recovery Point Objective (How far back you can go to retrieve data) 2 weeks/14 days

ArcGIS Enterprise Application Server Recovery Scenarios

In these scenarios, there is an assumption that the database and network are all up and running. The scenarios are defined as follows:

"Threat Level Yellow" One of the ArcGIS Servers is down, and users can work.

"Threat Level Orange" One of the ArcGIS Servers is down, and users are not able to continue to work.

"Threat Level Red" One of the Data Centers is down.

Problem If one of the ArcGIS servers are down, the GIS Enterprise will continue to work as the other server continues to process requests.
Identify

GIS team developed a script which is running as a Scheduled Job to monitor the services associated with these servers. If any of the components are not responding for more than 5 minutes, then the GIS team will get an email alert.

In addition, MDOT NOC is monitoring servers via the Orion Monitoring tool and alerts the TBU (MDTA Help Desk) that the server is down.
Resolution If at any point the server monitoring script detects that one of the servers is stopped or unresponsive, an email will be sent to the GIS team and it will be the responsibility of a GIS Administrator to understand the problem with the server and find a resolution.
Time to Recover If at any point the server monitoring script detects that one of the servers is stopped or unresponsive, an email will be sent to the GIS team and it will be the responsibility of a GIS Administrator to understand the problem with the server and find a resolution.
Data Loss None
Problem

If the ArcGIS datastore is down, the GIS enterprise will have issues as it is configured as a hosting serverforArcGIS Enterpriseto allow portal members topublish hosted feature layersoradd files tothe map viewer.

It will appear that everything is working, and the end user there is no connectivity to the data. User will not be able to do their work.
Identify

GIS team developed a script which is running as a Scheduled Job to monitor the services associated with these servers. If any of the components are not responding for more than 5 minutes, then the GIS team will get an email alert.

In addition, MDOT NOC is monitoring servers via the Orion Monitoring tool and alerts the TBU (MDTA Help Desk) that the server is down.
Resolution There are several ways to resolve this issue. The best way would be to install and configure one other relational data store with the same GIS server site, making this second relational data store machine as a standby machine. Hosted feature layer data is replicated from the primary to the standby.
Time to Recover

If we decide to have a standby data store, then there is no impact. But, if both primary and standby are down, then install the ArcGIS Data Store on a new machine and restore the latest available full back up using the restoredatastore utility.

The server can be restored to within 24 hours of the last backup. All servers are replicated to their alternate data center. Replicated backups can be used to restore in a 2-4-hour time period if isolated to a single server.
Data Loss None
Problem If ArcGIS portal is down, the GIS enterprise is down. No users can access the system to do their work.
Identify

GIS team developed a script which is running as a Scheduled Job to monitor the services associated with these servers. If any of the components are not responding for more than 5 minutes, then the GIS team will get an email alert.

In addition, MDOT NOC is monitoring servers via the Orion Monitoring tool and alerts the TBU (MDTA Help Desk) that the server is down.
Resolution

Sometimes after the restart of the server, it's possible that service may not restart on its own. If that's the case, it can be manually restarted.

If the problem is much bigger and the portal server itself is not responsive, there can be two scenarios:

  1. If the server does not comeback after it was restarted, the systems team can try to restart.
  2. If the server is completely unresponsive, then we need a plan to restore the last backup of the server to a new server with the identical name and static IPs.
Time to Recover

If scenario ‘2' above occurs, then we would need to work with the systems team to identify the total time they would need to restore a server to a new server.

Server can be restored to within 24 hours of the last backup.

All servers are replicated to their alternate data center.

A replicated backup can be used to restore in a 2-4-hour time period if isolated to single server.

Data Loss Possible portal content could be lost depending on the last backup available for the servers.
Problem If both ArcGIS servers are down, the GIS enterprise is down. Users are not able to use the system.
Identify

GIS team developed a script which is running as a Scheduled Job to monitor the services associated with these servers. If any of the components are not responding for more than 5 minutes, then the GIS team will get an email alert.

In addition, MDOT NOC is monitoring servers via the Orion Monitoring tool and alerts the TBU (MDTA Help Desk) that the server is down.
Resolution

Sometimes after the restart of the server, it is possible that services may not restart on their own. If that's the case it can be manually restarted.

If the problem is much bigger and the portal server itself is not responsive, there can be two scenarios:

  1. If the servers don't comeback after it was restarted, the systems team can try to restart.
  2. If both the servers are completely unresponsive then we need a plan to restore the last backup of the server to a new server with the identical name and static IPs. We will need to work with systems team to identify the total time they would need to restore a server, so that the users can be notified appropriately.
Time to Recover

If scenario '2' above occurs, then we would need to work with systems team to identify the total time they would need to restore at least one ArcGIS server.

The server can be restored to within 24 hours of the last backup.

All servers are replicated to their alternate data center.

A replicated backup can be used to restore in a 2-4-hour time period if isolated to single server.

Data Loss

Depends on the last backup available for the servers.

Possible portal content could be lost depending on the last backup available for the servers.

Problem If all the servers are down, the GIS enterprise is down. Both the ICC and JFK sites are down. System will take time to return to normal operations.If all the servers are down, the GIS enterprise is down. Both the ICC and JFK sites are down. System will take time to return to normal operations.
Identify

GIS team developed a script which is running as a Scheduled Job to monitor the services associated with these servers. If any of the components are not responding for more than 5 minutes, then the GIS team will get an email alert.

In addition, MDOT NOC is monitoring servers via the Orion Monitoring tool and alerts the TBU (MDTA Help Desk) that the server is down.
Resolution

If it's a restart issue, it can be resolved easily.

If the problem is that none of the servers are responding, there can be two scenarios:

  1. If the servers don't comeback after it was restarted, the systems team can try to restart.
  2. b. If the servers are completely unresponsive then we need a plan to restore the last backup of the server to a new server with the identical name and static IPs. We will need to work with systems team to identify the total time they would need to restore a server, so that the users can be notified appropriately.
Time to Recover

If scenario '2' above occurs, then we would need to work with systems team to identify the total time they would need to restore at least one of the ArcGIS servers, ArcGIS Portal and Primary Data Store.

The server can be restored to within 24 hours of the last backup.

All servers are replicated to their alternate data center.

A replicated backup can be used to restore in a 2–4-hour time period if isolated to single server.

Data Loss

Depends on the last backup available for the servers.

Possible portal content could be lost depending on the last backup available for the servers.

Problem If there is an issue with the web adaptor server, external users won't be able to get to the GIS Enterprise. Internal users would be able to access GIS but would need to directly use the URL for the server where portal is installed.
Identify

GIS team developed a script which is running as a Scheduled Job to monitor the services associated with these servers. If any of the components are not responding for more than 5 minutes, then the GIS team will get an email alert.

In addition, MDOT NOC is monitoring servers via the Orion Monitoring tool and alerts the TBU (MDTA Help Desk) that the server is down.
Resolution

If there is no response continuously for more than 5 minutes, we can try manually pinging the server. If there is still no response, we will need to bring it to TSO's attention immediately.

If for some reason the problem is only with the Web Adaptor server and not within the DMZ, we can quickly install the Web Adaptors (if the server cannot be recovered) on a new server and work with TSO to configure it.

Backups are performed at 1:35 AM nightly by the TSO group on the production servers and are available for 35 days.

Time to Recover We will need to work with TSO to find out the down time if we must reinstall and configure the web adaptors. The installation and configuration time from GIS team side would be 30 minutes.
Data Loss None
Problem Something has occurred to make the ICC Data Center unreachable, and the problem cannot be resolved in 24 hours and the GIS users are unable to do any work.
Identify

GIS team developed a script which is running as a Scheduled Job to monitor the services associated with these servers. If any of the components are not responding for more than 5 minutes, then the GIS team will get an email alert.

In addition, MDOT NOC is monitoring servers via the Orion Monitoring tool and alerts the TBU (MDTA Help Desk) that the server is down.
Resolution Fail over to the JFK Data Center. This includes standing up the ICC Servers at this site, restoring from backup, and validating the system is functional before turning it over to the users.
Time to Recover The server can be restored to within 24 hours of the last backup.
Data Loss None
Problem Something has occurred to make the JFK Data Center unreachable, and the problem cannot be resolved in 24 hours and the GIS users are unable to do any work.
Identify

GIS team developed a script which is running as a Scheduled Job to monitor the services associated with these servers. If any of the components are not responding for more than 5 minutes, then the GIS team will get an email alert.

In addition, MDOT NOC is monitoring servers via the Orion Monitoring tool and alerts the TBU (MDTA Help Desk) that the server is down.
Resolution Fail over to the ICC Data Center. This includes standing up the JFK Server at this site, restoring from backup, and validating the system is functional before turning it over to the users.
Time to Recover The server can be restored to within 24 hours of the last backup.
Data Loss None

RTO of the Database

Problem Data loss has occurred within a SQL database. This data loss can occur due to the accidental deletion of a table, accidental overwrite/modification of data in a table or through a general "corruption" of a table/database. This is usually a human error and may not be discovered for a few days.
Identify GIS power-users (data managers/publishers) will alert the GIS team via email with a Service Ticket to the MDTA Help Desk if a database has become unresponsive, providing the SQL Server Instance and the name of the database, the affected table/tables, and the best estimated date/time prior to the issue so that a proper restore point can be identified.
Resolution

The GIS Administrator will perform a quick diagnostic before communicating the issue to the DBA team.

A Service Request (SR) will be submitted to the MDTA_Help Desk via e-mail with a copy to the DBA Team.

Depending on the issue, the DBA team may be requested to:

  1. Restore the entire affected database to the identified restore point. or
  2. Provide a restored copy of the affected database according to the identified restore point. The data manager will manually update tables/records in the affected database to address the issue. (this should be done in the test environment.)
Time to Recover The GIS team will work with the DBA team to recover the database as quickly as possible, the DBA team will turnaround within one (1) hour from the time these requests are received.
Data Loss

Depending on the problem.

Two full backups are performed at 7:00 am and 7:00 pm, with hourly transactional backups in between.

One or two nodes being down will not cause any data lose due to replication on the cluster

Problem Any database has become unresponsive, meaning it is not responding to requests or login attempts.
Identify GIS power-users (data managers/publishers) will alert the GIS team via email with a Service Ticket to the MDTA Help Desk if a database has become unresponsive, providing the SQL Server Instance and the name of the database, the affected table/tables, and the best estimated date/time prior to the issue so that a proper restore point can be identified.
Resolution

The GIS Administrator will perform a quick diagnostic before communicating the issue to the DBA team.

A Service Request (SR) will be submitted to the MDTA_Help Desk via e-mail with a copy to the DBA Team.

Depending on the issue, the DBA team may be requested to:

  1. Restore the entire affected database to the identified restore point. or
  2. Provide a restored copy of the affected database according to the identified restore point. The data manager will manually update tables/records in the affected database to address the issue. (this should be done in the test environment.)
Time to Recover The GIS team will work with the DBA team to recover the database as quickly as possible, the DBA team will turnaround within one (1) hour from the time these requests are received.
Data Loss

Depending on the problem.

Two full backups are performed at 7:00 am and 7:00 pm, with hourly transactional backups in between.

One or two nodes being down will not cause any data lose due to replication on the cluster

Synchronous updating is used to keep the ICC databases always synchronized in real time.

Database resources will instantly transition from primary to secondary replica should the primary go down. Node and file-share majority is used to establish quorum for the node that owns and serves the database(s).

An AAG listener is used to abstract client connectivity thereby keeping failover and failback transparent to users, even during maintenance windows.

Failover and failback (at ICC) typically take less than 50 seconds to complete since both nodes are within the same datacenter.

RTO of 60 minutes or less can be established as a reasonable time required to get the GIS database back up and running at JFK from the time a human or natural disaster strikes the main servers at ICC.

The other secondary replica at JFK will be configured for asynchronous updating (latency factor TBD based on traffic volume and available bandwidth).

Asynchronous updating means manual intervention will be required to fail database resources ICC to JFK in case of a disaster.

If synchronization is configured to run every 15 or 30 minutes, for instance, a blackout at ICC may imply the capability to recover within 15 to 30 minutes of the time failure occurred. This will be further mitigated by the application of any transaction logs that occurred at ICC after the last point of synchronization at JFK.

The Disaster Recovery Plan (DRP) should take 24 hours to implement after the approval and initial execution.

Disaster Recovery Procedures

A disaster recovery procedure (DRP) will only be initiated if multiple/full systems are down at ICC due to a "disaster" event and systems cannot be recovered from backups within ICC. Once the DRP has been initiated, an implementation team for GIS will need the following, at a minimum, for recovery:

  1. Systems Engineer (s) with knowledge of SRM, MDTA Server and Storage Architecture, Active Directory and Group Policy.
  2. Systems/Solution Administrator with knowledge of ArcGIS, GIS Portal, and ArcGIS Server.
  3. Database Administrator with knowledge of GIS SQL Cluster
  4. An end user representative from MDTA OEC and Operations to test GIS software after recovery

Recovery Operations in Detail

This section will walk through the sequential actions the technical teams will need to perform in order to failover to the JFK Disaster Recovery Data Center.

  1. Data Center Team verifies if any of the ICC Data Center Systems are still reachable. This should have already been done as a part of the assessment of the DRT in their decision to activate the DRP.
  2. Data Center and Systems Teams verify that Priority 0 infrastructure systems are running and accessible at JFK site. If there are issues with the infrastructure systems those would have to be resolved prior to continuing with the procedures below.
  3. Data Center and Systems Teams verify that the JFK CIFS shares are accessible. (See #2)
  4. Systems Team will modify DNS record for \\cifsiccvfiler1\ to redirect to \\cifsjfkvfiler1\
  5. Database Team performs manual failover the database clusters.

    a. DBA recovers the DB Instances onto the JFK SQL nodes.

    b. Bring up the SQL cluster at JFK. PowerShell Commands once ICC is down - see below using ArcGIS Enterprise 10.9.16 as an example.

    Step

    Action

    1

    RDP into SQL21 at JFK

    2

    Start an elevated Windows PowerShell via Run as Administrator, and execute the following in order to Join SQL21 into the cluster:

    Start-ClusterNode -Name " MDTAGISSQL21" –FixQuorum

    3

    Confirm that Cluster has started on SQL21

    Get-ClusterNode -Name " MDTAGISSQL21"

    4

    With the cluster service started, voting rights for the nodes can be adjusted. If the remote node does not have a vote, then it will need to be configured to have a vote.

    (Get-ClusterNode -Name " MDTAGISSQL21").NodeWeight=1

    5

    Verify the votes on all the cluster nodes

    Get-ClusterNode | fl Name, NodeWeight

    6

    Once the remote node has been granted a vote for quorum, then remove the votes of the 2 nodes in the primary datacenter

    (Get-ClusterNode -name "MDTAGISSQL19").NodewWeight=0

    (Get-ClusterNode -name " MDTAGISSQL20").NodewWeight=0

    Get-ClusterNode | fl Name, NodeWeightGet

    7

    Launch Cluster Manager a verify SQL19 and SQL20are down and SQL21 is up

    8

    Start SQL Server Management Studio then open a query window

    9

    Execute the below command:
    ALTER AVAILABILITY GROUP GIS_AAGL2 FORCE_FAILOVER_ALLOW_DATA_LOSS

    This should recover the databases and leave them in a synchronized state and ready for use.

    10

    Execute the below against GISPROD and the two SIB databases:

    use [MDTAPUBWEBSQL]; 
    EXEC sp_change_users_login 'Update_One', 'maxuser', 'maxuser'
    go

    use [MDTAPUBWEBSQL];
    EXEC sp_change_users_login 'Update_One', 'maxuser', 'maxuser'
    go

    use [MDTAPUBWEBSQL];
    EXEC sp_change_users_login 'Update_One', 'maxuser', 'maxuser'
    go

    c. Verify the Listener on SQL Server at JFK is running.

    d. Shut down any DB clusters at ICC (if available).

  6. Data Center Team will log into the vCenter server at JFK and execute the MDTA DR Recovery Plan in SRM.
    1. SRM will shut down all applications servers at ICC (if available).
    2. SRM will try to perform one last storage snapshot at ICC (if available).
    3. SRM will attempt to shut down any servers at ICC (if available)
    4. SRM will recover all servers at JFK based on priority rules (see table below):
      1. Priority 1 - Database Servers
      2. Priority 2 - Management Servers
      3. Priority 3 - Mission Critical Application Servers
        1. AOC
        2. Police
        3. Maximo
        4. Finance
      4. Priority 4 - All other App Servers includes GIS Servers
      5. Priority 5 - All other Web Servers includes GIS DMZ Servers
    5. See below for SRM Recovery Plan tasks.

Recovery Plan Steps for GIS Servers

Once the DRP has been initiated, an implementation team for ArcGIS Enterprise 10.9.1 will need the following, at a minimum, for recovery:

  • Systems Engineer (s) with knowledge of SRM, MDTA Server and Storage Architecture, Active Directory and Group Policy.
  • Systems/Solution Administrator with knowledge of IIS and ArcGIS Enterprise 10.9.1
  • Database Administrator with knowledge of GIS SQL Cluster
  • An end user representative from MDTA Operations to test ArcGIS Enterprise software after recovery

The following steps should be followed to recovery GIS in a disaster situation:

  1. Take a snapshot of the GIS database cluster.
  2. Verify if any of the SQL servers in the GIS cluster are still up and running. If they are still reachable, DBA to perform on last DB sync before failing over.
  3. Bring down the database host.
  4. Take a snapshot of the GIS server.
  5. Take a snapshot of the production and test clusters.
  6. Manually failover the database. This needs to be done manually due to A.D. synchronization.
  7. Shut down the GIS cluster at ICC.
  8. A Systems Engineer will remote into VCenter at JFK and activate the SRM Protection Plan.
  9. Shut down all applications servers at ICC.
  10. The Systems Engineer will verify all GIS systems are down at ICC
    1. Verify that the clusters are down.
    2. Verify that the database is down.
    3. Verify that IIS is down in DMZ.
  11. Verify that infrastructure systems such as Active Directory, DNS & VMware are up and running at the JFK site.
  12. The SRM will pause so that the DBA can recover the DB Instance onto the JFK SQL node on mdtagissql21.
  13. Bring up the SQL cluster at JFK. PowerShell Commands once ICC is down (script mentioned above)
    Steps to modify the variables on the application for the Attachment Directory - Process 1

    Step

    Action

    1

    Remote desktop to MDTAGISDSTORE

    2

    Open the Notepad as administrator and edit the file C:\inetpub\wwwroot\MDTAFileShareSvc\web.config

    3

    Change key <sourcePath " \\cifsiccvfiler1\MDTAGIS\Data "> to "\\cifsjfkvfiler1\MDTAGIS\Data "
  14. SRM will try to perform one last storage snapshot at ICC.
  15. SRM will shut down the following application servers at ICC:
    1. The Solutions Administrator will RDP into Deployment Manager Server and start services at JFK in proper sequence as defined by the GIS Support Documentation.
    2. Update the properties files on the web servers (for attachments).
    3. Data center Team can force DNS replication if necessary to speed up the recovery time.
    4. Verify that IIS is up and running.
    5. Need to use IP address is the DNS sync doesn't work quickly. Otherwise this will take about 15 minutes. (May need to Flush and re-register the DNS.)
    6. The Solutions Administrator will perform functionality tests with user(s).
    7. Notify users that GIS is up and running.

NOTE: At the writing of this document, Rubrik AppFlow is in use at MDTA. Rubrik AppFlow has the capability of restoring an entire application Architecture once blueprint of the GIS application is setup. This includes the SQL Servers and will also require those servers to be setup and backup using the Rubric AppFlow Tool.

// First obtain the X and Y coordinates and the spatial reference // from the feature's Geometry and store them as variables. var PointGeometry = Geometry($feature); if (PointGeometry != null){ var ArcadeX = PointGeometry.x; var ArcadeY = PointGeometry.y; var ArcadeSr = PointGeometry.spatialReference.wkid; var Latitude, Longitude; } if (PointGeometry == null){ var ArcadeX = 0; var ArcadeY = 0; var ArcadeSr = 0; var Latitude, Longitude; } // Check the spatial reference system of the web map to see if the // coordinates need converting to Lat and Long for use by Google. // If the web map is in Web Mercator (102100) then the coordinates // will be converted to Lat and Long. // If the web map is in WGS84 (4326) then no conversion necessary // since the feature coordinates will already be in Lat and Long. function AuxSphereToLatLon(x, y) { Console("Converting..."); // Conversion based on http://dotnetfollower.com/wordpress/2011/07/javascript-how-to-convert-mercator-sphere-coordinates-to-latitude-and-longitude/ var rMajor = 6378137; var shift = PI * rMajor; Longitude = x / shift * 180.0; Latitude = y / shift * 180.0; Latitude = 180 / PI * (2 * Atan(Exp(Latitude * PI / 180.0)) - PI / 2.0); } if (ArcadeSr == 4326) { Console("4326 Spatial Reference - No Conversion Necessary"); Latitude = ArcadeY; Longitude = ArcadeX; } else if (ArcadeSr == 102100) { Console("102100 Spatial Reference - Conversion Necessary"); AuxSphereToLatLon(ArcadeX, ArcadeY); } else { Console(ArcadeSr + " Spatial Reference is not supported - currently works with Web Maps where the basemap is in WGS84 (4326) or Web Mercator Auxiliary Sphere 102100"); } // Build url var url = "http://maps.google.com/maps?q=&layer=c&cbll=" + text(Latitude) + "," + text(Longitude); // var url = "https://www.bing.com/maps?&style=x&cp=" + text(Latitude) + "~" + text(Longitude); return url;

Google Street View Points

function MetersToLatLon(x, y) { // Converts XY point from Spherical Mercator EPSG:3857(Web Mercator Auxiliary Sphere) to lat/lon in WGS84 Datum (EPSG:4326). // Source: http://www.maptiler.org/google-maps-coordinates-tile-bounds-projection/ var originShift = 2.0 * PI * 6378137.0 / 2.0; var lon = (x / originShift) * 180.0; var lat = (y / originShift) * 180.0; lat = 180.0 / PI * (2.0 * Atan( Exp( lat * PI / 180.0)) - PI / 2.0); return [lat, lon]; } function FormatLatLon(lat, lon) { var url = lat + "," + lon;// This is the line that defines the location Console(url); return url; } var latlon = MetersToLatLon(Geometry($feature).X, Geometry($feature).Y); var url = FormatLatLon(latlon[0], latlon[1]); return url;

Feature XY Points

function MetersToLatLon(x, y) { // Converts XY point from Spherical Mercator EPSG:3857(Web Mercator Auxiliary Sphere) to lat/lon in WGS84 Datum (EPSG:4326). // Source: http://www.maptiler.org/google-maps-coordinates-tile-bounds-projection/ var originShift = 2.0 * PI * 6378137.0 / 2.0; var lon = (x / originShift) * 180.0; var lat = (y / originShift) * 180.0; lat = 180.0 / PI * (2.0 * Atan( Exp( lat * PI / 180.0)) - PI / 2.0); return [lat, lon]; } function FormatLatLon(lat, lon) { var url = lat + "," + lon;// This is the line that defines the location Console(url); return url; } var latlon = MetersToLatLon(Geometry($feature).X, Geometry($feature).Y); var url = latlon[0]+" "+latlon[1]; return url;

FeatureXY - PassField

// First obtain the X and Y coordinates and the spatial reference // from the feature's Geometry and store them as variables. // For line and polygons, obtain centroid of the feature var PointGeometry = Centroid(Geometry($feature)); if (PointGeometry != null){ var ArcadeX = PointGeometry.x; var ArcadeY = PointGeometry.y; var ArcadeSr = PointGeometry.spatialReference.wkid; var Latitude, Longitude; } if (PointGeometry == null){ var ArcadeX = 0; var ArcadeY = 0; var ArcadeSr = 0; var Latitude, Longitude; } // Check the spatial reference system of the web map to see if the // coordinates need converting to Lat and Long for use by Google. // If the web map is in Web Mercator (102100) then the coordinates // will be converted to Lat and Long. // If the web map is in WGS84 (4326) then no conversion necessary // since the feature coordinates will already be in Lat and Long. function AuxSphereToLatLon(x, y) { Console("Converting..."); // Conversion based on http://dotnetfollower.com/wordpress/2011/07/javascript-how-to-convert-mercator-sphere-coordinates-to-latitude-and-longitude/ var rMajor = 6378137; var shift = PI * rMajor; Longitude = x / shift * 180.0; Latitude = y / shift * 180.0; Latitude = 180 / PI * (2 * Atan(Exp(Latitude * PI / 180.0)) - PI / 2.0); } if (ArcadeSr == 4326) { Console("4326 Spatial Reference - No Conversion Necessary"); Latitude = ArcadeY; Longitude = ArcadeX; } else if (ArcadeSr == 102100) { Console("102100 Spatial Reference - Conversion Necessary"); AuxSphereToLatLon(ArcadeX, ArcadeY); } else { Console(ArcadeSr + " Spatial Reference is not supported - currently works with Web Maps where the basemap is in WGS84 (4326) or Web Mercator Auxiliary Sphere 102100"); } // Build url var url = text(Latitude) + "," + text(Longitude); return url;

Centroid XY - Lines and Polygons

function MetersToLatLon(x, y) { // Converts XY point from Spherical Mercator EPSG:3857(Web Mercator Auxiliary Sphere) to lat/lon in WGS84 Datum (EPSG:4326). // Source: http://www.maptiler.org/google-maps-coordinates-tile-bounds-projection/ var originShift = 2.0 * PI * 6378137.0 / 2.0; var lon = (x / originShift) * 180.0; var lat = (y / originShift) * 180.0; lat = 180.0 / PI * (2.0 * Atan( Exp( lat * PI / 180.0)) - PI / 2.0); return [lat, lon]; } function FormatLatLon(lat, lon) { var url = lat + "," + lon;// This is the line that defines the location Console(url); return url; } var latlon = []; var PointGeometry = Geometry($feature); if (PointGeometry == null){ var ArcadeX = 0; var ArcadeY = 0; var ArcadeSr = 0; } else { var ArcadeX = Geometry($feature).X; var ArcadeY = Geometry($feature).Y; var ArcadeSr = PointGeometry.spatialReference.wkid; } Console('Converting XY: ', ArcadeX) if (ArcadeSr == 4326) { Console("4326 Spatial Reference - No Conversion Necessary"); latlon = [ArcadeY, ArcadeX]; } else if (ArcadeSr == 102100) { Console("102100 Spatial Reference - Conversion Necessary"); latlon = MetersToLatLon(ArcadeX, ArcadeY); } else { Console(ArcadeSr + " Spatial Reference is not supported - currently works with Web Maps where the basemap is in WGS84 (4326) or Web Mercator Auxiliary Sphere 102100"); latlon = [0,0]; } // var latlon = MetersToLatLon(Geometry($feature).X, Geometry($feature).Y); var url = FormatLatLon(latlon[0], latlon[1]); return url;

Introduction to ArcGIS Pro ArcGIS Pro is a full-featured professional desktop GIS application from Esri. With ArcGIS Pro, you can explore, visualize, and analyze data; create 2D maps and 3D scenes; and share your work to ArcGIS Online or your ArcGIS Enterprise portal. The sections within introduce the sign-in process, the start page, ArcGIS Pro projects, and the user interface. All links will open in a new page/tab. The right button will take you to the latest version's (currently 3.1) reference material. The left button willl take you to the current MDTA version's reference material - 2.9. 2.9 Latest (3.1) Maps in ArcGIS Pro Mapping in ArcGIS Pro is a visual and interactive experience. You can create 2D maps and 3D scenes to visualize spatial data. Organize and customize the display of one or more layers to be as simple or complex as the data requires. 2.9 Latest (3.1) Spatial analysis in ArcGIS Pro Spatial analysis allows you to solve complex location-oriented problems, explore and understand your data from a geographic perspective, determine relationships, detect and quantify patterns, assess trends, and make predictions and decisions. Spatial analysis goes beyond mapping and allows you to study the characteristics of places and the relationships among them. Spatial analysis lends new perspectives to your decision-making. Using data engineering, you can explore, visualize, clean, and prepare your data. Visualizing data using charts can uncover data patterns, trends, relationships, and structures that may otherwise be difficult to see as raw numbers in a table. Machine learning refers to a set of data-driven algorithms and techniques that automate the prediction, classification, and clustering of data. Deep Learning is an important subset of machine learning techniques that uses artificial neural networks to learn from data. ArcGIS Pro includes tools that can transform large amounts of spatial data into manageable information using Big data analytics. Information on Modeling/Scripting and sharing/collabortion are also discssed, and will also have their own reference/tutorial section(s). 2.9 Latest (3.1) Share your work in ArcGIS Pro ArcGIS Pro provides numerous options for sharing your work. 2.9 Latest (3.1) Data in ArcGIS Pro GIS data represents real-world objects and events, and the things we know about them. ArcGIS Pro is designed to handle many types of data for many different purposes. You can work with feature- and raster-based spatial data stored in geodatabases and other formats, tabular data in stored spreadsheets or other files, web layers and services hosted in portals or servers, and data you collect and create yourself. Other references/tutorials relating to data can be found throughtout the MDTA Knowldege Base Site. 2.9 Latest (3.1) ArcGIS Pro Python Reference The ArcGIS Pro Python reference contains detailed information about every ArcPy module, function, and class provided with ArcGIS Pro; working with Python; and working with, and creating your own, geoprocessing tools in Python. 2.9 Latest (3.1) ArcGIS Pro Geoprocessing Tool References The ArcGIS Pro geoprocessing tool reference contains detailed information about every geoprocessing tool provided with ArcGIS Pro as well as the environment settings that can be applied to them and any errors or warnings that may be encountered as you use them. Note that some geoprocessing tools require either an Advanced ArcGIS Pro License and/or one-or-more extension licences. 2.9 Latest (3.1) ArcGIS Pro Licensing After ArcGIS Pro is installed on a machine, it is enabled for use when it can get a valid license. ArcGIS Pro can be configured to use different license types. Depending on the license type, licenses are authorized, managed, and validated by ArcGIS Pro in different ways. ArcGIS Pro extension products integrate seamlessly with the core application to provide specialized functionality. Extensions are licensed separately from the core application but must have the same license type as the core application with which they are used. 2.9 Latest (3.1)
